critical_code_review_comments: admin_erase_client in server.py: the anonymize UPDATE on clients + review_threads is not wrapped in a transaction. If the sb.auth.admin.update_user_by_id call fails, the DB rows are already anonymized while the auth account is still live — the raised 500 is honest but leaves partial state. Consider updating auth BEFORE the DB row (or using a Postgres function/RPC) so the flow is atomic.

admin_erase_client detects prior erasure via client['email'].startswith('erased-'). This is brittle — any future re-anonymization scheme that uses a different prefix will silently break idempotency. Prefer a dedicated boolean column (e.g. erased_at timestamp) or check the email suffix @anonymized.invalid as well.

review_threads author_name is set to 'Erased Client' only for rows where author_role='client'. Any legacy rows written before author_role was populated (nullable) would be missed. Consider dropping the author_role filter or coalescing.
Password rotation uses secrets.token_urlsafe(24) but the account is also banned for 100 years — belt-and-braces is fine, but note the new password is never surfaced anywhere, which is correct.
